item.title: GT Volleyball swept 3-0 by #2 Pitt
item.description: Magda Kobaidze up for a block | Danny Karnik - GTAA McCAMISH PAVILION — In their 2026 return to McCamish Pavilion, Georgia Tech volleyball had no answers for the best team in the ACC and #2 national ranked Pitt Panthers, losing in a 3-0 sweep (25-19, 25-13, 25-18). Tech generally had a very hard time getting around Pitt’s middle blockers with no hitters going over .200. Pitt finished with 13 total blocks to Tech’s 6. In three sets, Tech hit .055 overall, going as low as -.194 in the second set. Pitt brought their usual row of All-Americans, led by Olivia Babcock who tied the game lead with 12 kills, hitting .500 for the match. And it only gets harder. #7 SMU comes to town on Sunday afternoon, also in McCamish Pavilion. Set 1 Pitt took an early 3-0 lead and held their lead until a Magda Kobaidze kill tied it at 6-6. The ties lasted to 9-9 before Pitt broke open their lead again to 13-10, forcing Tech’s first timeout. With Alida Bennour at the service line after, she hit two aces and took advantage of a Blaire Bayless attack error to tie at 14-14. Pitt grabbed their advantage right back with Olivia Babcock at the service line to go up 17-14. They held a slight margin before two straight Zoë Humphrey points (kill and block) made it 19-18 Pitt, forcing the Panthers’ first timeout. Two straight Babcock kills after forced Tech’s final timeout down 21-18. An ace that clipped the tape by Ayanna Watson secured the set 25-19 for the Panthers Set 2 (1-0 Pitt) Pitt quickly dominated to start the set, driving away with a five point run with multiple blocks to go up 7-3 and force Tech’s first timeout. Pitt did not relent, going on yet another three point run to go up 10-4, and then a third to go up 13-5 and force Tech’s last timeout of the set. Tech got out of the scoring run and got an ace from Vitoria Belfort on a spot serve, but only drew down double at 14-7. At the technical timeout, Tech was hitting -.286. Tech errors and Babcock kills continued to draw Tech out of the set, going behind 10 points multiple times. Pitt took the set 25-13, outhitting Tech .320 to -.194 in the set. Set 3 (2-0 Pitt) Tech sustained their first lead of the match early in the 3rd, getting a three point run with a Garibaldi block to go up 3-1. After Pitt tied it, Tech regained a two point lead on a Kobaidze kill that found its way through a triple block. Pitt then went on three then five point runs to go up 12-7. Tech climbed back within two to 12-10 before Pitt went on a 9-2 run, during which Humphrey went out with what appeared to be an ankle injury. Down 20-14, Bennour was back on the service line and hit her fourth ace of the match followed by a Bieleski kill for a three point run, forcing Pitt’s first timeout of the set. item.title: Brandeis quarterback Wynter Smith voted Express-News Athlete of the Week
item.description: Brandeis' Wynter Smith rolls out of the pocket during the third quarter of a District 28-6A football game against Roosevelt on Thursday, October 15, 2026 at Farris Stadium in San Antonio. (Charlie Blalock/For the Express-News) Brandeis quarterback Wynter Smith put on a record-breaking performance last week in helping the Broncos to a key win over Roosevelt. That star effort now has earned him Express-News Athlete of the Week honors. The senior rushed 19 times for 153 yards and six touchdowns in the 49-28 victory, breaking the school record for touchdowns in a single game. He also threw for 73 yards and another score on 7-of-10 passing in keeping the Broncos in the thick of the playoff chase in District 28-6A. He continued his stellar play Thursday in a 51-35 win over Madison, rushing for 232 yards and three touchdowns on 23 carries and completing 8 of 14 passes for 140 yards and two touchdowns. Mere hours after his performance against the Mavericks, the Athlete of the Week poll closed with Smith beating out four fellow finalists from last week's games. HS FOOTBALL SCOREBOARD: Check out San Antonio's final scores and stats for Week 9 Pieper junior quarterback Lance Reid, who was a backup a few weeks ago, threw for 482 yards and six touchdowns on 19-of-27 passing in Pieper's 62-31 win over East Central. The win moved the Warriors into a tie for second place in 27-6A with the Hornets, and Reid was named Offensive Player of the Week. Picking up his second Defensive Player of the Week honor this season, Steele senior Pike Kempe recorded 15 tackles in a 57-12 win over Judson. He had 2½ tackles for loss, one sack, one quarterback hurry and one pass breakup. The Volleyball Player of the Week, Highlands junior Riley Reyes, combined for 72 assists in victories against Edison and Jefferson. She averaged over 10 assists per set to help the Owls clinch the District 27-5A championship. She had 42 assists against Edison and 30 assists and 20 digs against Jefferson. Boerne Champion junior Brady Cooksey had 73 assists, 40 digs, six aces, five blocks and eight kills against South San and McCollum. The two wins put the Chargers into a tie for first, setting up a showdown with 26-5A co-leader Boerne. The Chargers swept the Greyhounds on Tuesday to claim the inside track to an outright district title. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Tricolor face Mirassol in Brasileirão clash in inland São Paulo
item.description: Tricolor face Mirassol in Brasileirão clash in inland São Paulo Buoyed by back-to-back wins over Vitória (2–1) and Vasco da Gama (1–0), Tricolor will face Mirassol this Saturday afternoon (24) at 4:30 p.m. at José Maria de Campos Maia Stadium, in the 32nd round of the Brazilian Championship. “Those were two hard-earned wins built on solid performances. That was what we expected, because we worked for it. We’ve managed to stay mentally strong and focused on the upcoming games, because there are seven important rounds left to keep this going,” said right-back Pedro Lima. São Paulo sits ninth in the Brasileirão, with 42 points from 31 games. Meanwhile, the team from the interior of São Paulo state is in 14th place with 36 points. “Mirassol has its strengths, but we’ve trained hard. We’re ready. We have 100% confidence in every player here and in the game plan the coach has laid out for us. We’re focused, 100% prepared and confident that we can bring the three points home,” added the number 32. In 21 meetings with Mirassol, São Paulo has recorded 13 wins, four draws and four defeats. The teams have met 11 times at José Maria de Campos Maia, with six wins for Tricolor, three draws and two defeats. In the Brasileirão, they have faced each other just three times: one win for São Paulo and two for Mirassol. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Texans Announce Critical Tank Dell Update Amid Significant Roster News
item.description: The Texans confirmed encouraging news for Tank Dell. Getty The Houston Texans’ wait for Tank Dell appears set to end. The Texans released their final injury report of Week 7 after practice on Friday, and Dell–who was a full participant in all three sessions this week–was listed as “questionable” to face the New York Giants. Houston will also have Azeez Al-Shaair, Dalton Schultz, and Trent Brown against the Giants, despite all three starters missing some time during the week of preparation. Two more days until #Texans receiver Tank Dell first #NFL game in nearly two years pic.twitter.com/Szax4SWEbR — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) October 23, 2026 Dell’s return is highly anticipated, and Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said it would happen. A third-round pick in the 2023 draft (No. 69 overall), Dell has been sidelined since Week 16 of the 2024 season, when teammate Jared Wayne collided with his knee on an attempted touchdown reception. Dell tore multiple ligaments and suffered a dislocated kneecap. He has been grinding to get back on the field in a competitive game ever since. The Texans have kept expectations for Dell to a minimum. They just want him to be himself and get back into the flow of things after such a long layoff. It remains to be seen just how much of a workload he gets if he plays, but it will not be close to a full allotment of snaps. Regardless, this is great news for Dell and the Texans, who need it with several other starters not playing this week. Tank Dell News Helps After Texans’ Announcement As the injury report revealed, while Dell could be back in action, the Texans remain without running back David Montgomery (groin), nickelback Jalen Pitre (shoulder), both of whom have been out since Week 5. Moreover, safety Reed Blankenship is out due to the concussion he suffered in Week 6. The Texans are also going to be without reserve lineman Blake Fisher, who has played a role as an additional lineman in jumbo packages. Houston #Texans Friday Injury Report & Game Status Report for Week 7 vs. the New York Giants: pic.twitter.com/JVPJeznQKU — Houston Texans PR (@TexansPR) October 23, 2026 The Texans are 2-4 and looking to get themselves back into the playoff race in the AFC. Another win–their third straight–would go a long way. That is even against an opponent from the NFC in the visiting Giants. item.description: Mixed martial artists have endured some gnarly injuries throughout the years, but it’s rare that a fighter is left reeling in pain from something a referee does. Unfortunately for one unlucky fighter, that’s exactly what happened during Friday’s Top FC 24 event in Seoul, South Korea. item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos reacts to a call against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) Getty Sometimes it’s not about the money — Denver Broncos stars Jaylen Waddle and Quinn Meinerz have plenty of that — it’s about the principle of the matter. “Per sources, Broncos RG Quinn Meinerz and WR Jaylen Waddle both had their $14,926 dice roll celebration fines dismissed upon appeal,” 9News Denver’s Mike Klis wrote on his official X account on Friday. “BREAKING: Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle and RG Quinn Meinerz were FINED $14,926 each by the NFL for their Yahtzee dice roll celebration during Week 3,” Football Forever wrote on X. “ Meinerz and Waddle pantomimed rolling dice after Waddle scored a 2-point try, and the NFL classified the celebration as illegal.” The Broncos, 4-2, travel to face the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in Week 7. item.title: How to Check if Your Next Slab Was Stolen in the 6,451-Card PSA Heist
item.description: Over 6,45 0 graded cards were recently stolen from a transport truck leaving PSA, marking one of the largest single thefts in the history of the sports card market. As outlined in PSA’s official theft update , this massive heist underscores a critical vulnerability in the secondary market. If the hobby wants to stop stolen goods from circulating freely, buyer behavior has to change immediately. As I previously covered in The Hobby’s Theft Crisis: How My Stolen Cards Ended Up in a High-End Repack , stolen slabs seamlessly re-enter the market because buyers and vendors rarely verify certification numbers before transacting. It is time to start checking cert numbers on every slab before completing a purchase. This is the single most effective action collectors can take; when buyers refuse to purchase unverified slabs, vendors are forced to be far more rigorous about vetting their sources. How to Check if a Card Was Stolen If you are purchasing a graded card on the secondary market, take these exact steps to ensure you are not buying stolen property from the recent heist or other thefts: Check the PSA Verification Tool: Enter the card’s certification number directly into the PSA lookup database ( psacard.com/cert ). PSA has officially deactivated the cert numbers for all 6,451 stolen cards, which will show the card as decertified if searched. Cross-Reference the Master List: PSA has published a complete PDF list of every deactivated certification number associated with the truck heist. You can manually check this master document before sending funds to a seller. Search TheGTCR.com: The Global Trading Card Registry acts as a centralized database where collectors, dealers, and victims of theft can immediately log stolen items. You can search any PSA, BGS, or CGC certification number or serial number to see if it has been reported. The platform also allows victims to upload high-resolution photos and document the exact circumstances of their loss. The site has already been updated to include all 6,451 stolen PSA cards. If you believe you have information that could aid the investigation, please contact the FBI or Santa Ana Police Department at +1 714-245-8345.

item.description: San Francisco 49ers player Christian Kirk catches a ball during football practice in Santa Clara, Calif., on May 28, 2026. (AP Photo/Jeff Chiu) This offseason, the 49ers signed two veteran wide receivers in free agency. It's quite clear already that they've struck gold with Mike Evans. But the other hasn't even suited up yet - and now, he's getting the spotlight. The 49ers will enter Sunday's matchup in Atlanta undefeated, but they're facing a borderline crisis at wideout. Pretty much every top receiver has missed time this season, and that now officially includes Evans, whom the team ruled out for Sunday's game with Achilles tendinitis. And so, with little room for error, the next man up is Christian Kirk. In true 2026 49ers fashion, Kirk is listed as questionable for the second straight week as he recovers from a calf injury he suffered in training camp, which led to his placement on injured reserve before the season started. Kirk returned to practice last week in a limited capacity but didn't play on Monday night. This week, he's been a full participant, despite the questionable tag, and quarterback Brock Purdy told reporters on Thursday that Kirk is "good to go now, man, in my eyes." The team also appears to think so, as the 49ers released defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo from their 53-man roster, clearing a roster spot that they would need in order to activate Kirk from injured reserve. Kirk, 29, is in his ninth NFL season and has played for three teams so far: the Cardinals, Jaguars and Texans. He's put up some big seasons in the past, particularly in a two-year run from 2021-2022, but has been more of a role player recently. Last year in Houston, he caught 28 passes for 239 yards and one touchdown in the regular season. He did have a big game in the playoffs for the Texans, tallying eight catches for 144 yards and a touchdown in a blowout win over the Steelers. Of course, at 5 feet, 11 inches, Kirk is not going to be a like-for-like fill-in for Evans. The 6-foot-5-inch future Hall of Famer has played through a number of ailments already this year while clearly never being fully healthy. With the bye week following this road game, the 49ers are electing to give Evans multiple weeks off in a row to try and get healthy. item.title: Mickey Guyton, in Brewers jersey, sings national anthem for Game 1 of World Series
item.description: Acclaimed country artist Mickey Guyton, in her first performance ever in Milwaukee, sang a stirring rendition of the National Anthem ahead of Game 1 of the World Series at American Family Field - while sporting a Brewers jersey. As Guyton's voice soared to rising cheers, fans in the stadium waved a massive American flag, with members of the Milwaukee Police Department standing in salute, and Valkyrie, a 15-year-old bald eagle from Milwaukee's Schlitz Audubon Nature Center, also on the field. Guyton was part of the pregame festivities that included people on the field coordinating card flips to map out key dates and logos for the postseason runs for the Milwaukee Brewers and their opponent the Tampa Bay Rays . item.description: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Bills S Sam Franklin’s suspension decreased to $14,926 fine for spitting incident appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Buffalo Bills safety and special teams captain Sam Franklin Jr. has successfully appealed his one-game suspension for allegedly spitting at an opponent during the team’s Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The NFL reduced his punishment to a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct, meaning he’s eligible to play when Buffalo returns from its bye week. The league announced the revised disciplinary decision on Friday following a review conducted by hearing officer James Thrash, who was jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFL Players Association. Franklin had initially faced a one-game suspension after the league alleged that he spat at a Raiders player after an extra-point attempt with 1:32 remaining in the fourth quarter of the Bills’ 33-30 win. Franklin denied the accusation and promptly appealed the suspension. His representatives, Harold C. Lewis and Christian Addison, also rejected the allegation, arguing that there was no evidence supporting the league’s initial decision. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The ruling means Franklin will remain available for Buffalo’s Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on November 1. The 30-year-old has recorded six tackles this season, all on special teams, across six appearances. He is in his second season with the Bills and his seventh NFL campaign. Across 97 career games, including nine starts, with Buffalo and the Carolina Panthers, he has accumulated 124 tackles and returned an interception 99 yards for a touchdown. Franklin was previously fined $9,425 for a blindside block in Week 1, making this his second fine of the 2026 season. Meanwhile, Buffalo will still be without safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, who was ejected during the second quarter versus Las Vegas after spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. item.title: Who is 'Front Row Amy?' Meet the Brewers superfan who sits behind home plate at nearly every home game
item.description: Who is 'Front Row Amy?' Meet the Brewers superfan who sits behind home plate at nearly every home game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With 162 regular season games, 81 played in home stadiums, the MLB season spans eight months of the year. When adorned in a unique outfit, repeat fans behind home plate can stick out. This is how the legend of 'Marlins Man' was born. He kept appearing all over MLB in his bright orange jersey, and fans took notice. 'M&Ms Guy' was another one who drew attention thanks to his M&M logo blazer when he attended Chicago White Sox games. The Milwaukee Brewers have their own super fan who sits behind home plate of most home games. Let's meet "Front Row Amy." MORE: MLB pitchers with 3,000 strikeouts Who is Front Row Amy? The legend of "Front Row Amy" grew by her simply being a consistent presence at games. Milwaukee fans took notice of a woman sitting by herself behind the plate at Brewers games. She always seemed to be there, with her scoring book, and fans always commented that it seemed like she never left her seat. The baseball fan multiverse had its "Avengers Assemble' moment at a playoff game in 2023 where 'Marlins Man', 'M&M's Guy' and 'Front Row Amy' were all sitting behind home plate. Front Row Amy next to Marlins Guy next to M&Ms Guy pic.twitter.com/Eny2WNCbfE — Drake Bentley (@DrakeBentleyMJS) October 3, 2023 In an interview with retired Milwaukee Journal Sentinel columnist Jim Stingl , 'Front Row Amy' found her love for the Brew Crew in 2007 and also that she preferred attending games alone while keeping the scorebook. The National Bobblehead Hall of fame honored her fandom with her own custom bobblehead . MORE: Oldest MLB players to play in a game What is Front Row Amy's real name? 'Front Row Amy's' real name is Amy Williams. She resides in Oshkosh, Wisconsin about an hour and a half from American Family Field in Milwaukee. She is married to her husband, Russ, and the two have three children together. MORE: Everything to know about the World Series trophy Where does Front Row Amy sit? 'Front Row Amy's' famous seat is Row 1, seat 5 in section 117. She began sitting there in 2011, after sitting in the fourth row of the same section in 2009 and 2010. When 'Front Row Amy' can't attend games, she will sell them through her X account/gmail or ticket re-sellers like StubHub. item.title: Fastest pitches in World Series history: Jacob Misiorowski breaks record on first pitch of Game 1
item.description: Fastest pitches in World Series history: Jacob Misiorowski breaks record on first pitch of Game 1 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Brewers are a spectacle of their own after returning to the World Series for the first time in 44 years, but the player that made fans tune into Friday's Game 1 was Jacob Misiorowski. The projected NL Cy Young Award winner was lethal in his first full season, posting a 1.80 ERA across 30 starts and blowing an otherworldly fastball by hitters from March to October. To no surprise, the list of the fastest pitches thrown in 2026 was littered with Misiorowski's name. The young ace averaged 100.6 MPH on his four-seam fastball and threw more than a dozen pitches of 104 MPH or faster during the regular season. On Friday, Misiorowski etched his name in World Series history. Here's what you need to know. MORE: Ranking the 12 best players in 2026 World Series Fastest pitch in World Series history Misiorowski threw a 103.5 MPH pitch for his very first pitch Friday's Game 1 to Tampa Bay's Yandy Diaz, breaking a record previously held by Aroldis Chapman. The fastest pitch in World Series history before tonight was 101.1 MPH. Jacob Misiorowski’s very first pitch of the game tonight? 103.5 MPH 🤯 https://t.co/MgAEOCYb3W — Just Baseball (@JustBB_Media) October 24, 2026 Chapman threw a 103.2 MPH pitch for the Cubs during the 2016 World Series, setting a record that stood for a decade. With Misiorowski and the Brewers reaching the Fall Classic, the chances of that mark holding up for another year were always going to be slim. While the record only traces back to the pitch-tracking era in 2008, it would be tough to imagine anyone in MLB history came particularly close to what Misiorowski or Chapman managed to throw. MORE: SN predicts the 2026 World Series Fastest pitch by a starter in World Series history Misiorowski had no problem shattering the previous record for fastest pitch by a starting pitcher in the World Series, which was Noah Syndergaard's 101.1 MPH pitch for the Mets in 2015. Before Friday, Syndergaard's 101.1 MPH pitch against the Royals was the only pitch of at least 101 MPH by a starter in World Series history. Misiorowski threw several pitches of at least 101 MPH and three of at least 102 MPH in the first inning alone in Game 1 against the Rays. item.description: The Browns pulled off the big win over the Baltimore Ravens last week to move to 2-0 in the division, 4-2 overall, and currently sit in first place in the AFC North. Week-to-week, fan confidence increased by 26 percentage points up to 85%, a new season high. item.description: Milwaukee Brewers shortstop Robin Yount, left, waves to the crowd as they celebrate near the dugout in County Stadium, Milwaukee after Game 5 of the World Series, Oct. 17, 1982. Thanks to the dear old Chron, I had the privilege of covering the 1982 American League Championship Series in that ballpark, and Milwaukee hasn't known anything like it since. The Brewers won that best-of-five series by sweeping the final three games at home against the California Angels, as they were then known, and the ensuing World Series (a loss to the Cardinals) was their last such appearance until Friday night's opener against the Tampa Bay Rays. To say the least, those days are fondly remembered around town. The Brewers' manager back then, Harvey Kuenn, was a Milwaukee guy, born and raised on the south side. He and his wife, Audrey, operated a neighborhood bar called Cesar's Inn, and whenever the Brewers had a home off-day during the postseason, you'd find him there, serving drinks and spinnin' yarns. The place was packed all week - "Harv and Aud's," they called it - and I became a regular with Bill Madden, the New York Daily News baseball writer bound for the Hall of Fame, and several other scribes. Watching Harvey hold court behind the bar, we marveled at the fact that he'd lost his right leg to an amputation just two years before. (He thought seriously about a wooden leg, but opted for a modern prosthetic.) Making the last out of Sandy Koufax' perfect game at Dodger Stadium in 1965, because I was there. And not to be forgotten, that Kuenn was a huge part of the 1962 San Francisco Giants' run to the World Series, hitting .304 in 130 games as an outfielder/third baseman. (Associated Press) Speaking of a long-ago era, the Brewers' most heroic starters during that three-game run were Don Sutton and Pete Vuckovich, neither of whom gave a damn about fastball velocity, radar gun readings or throwing every pitch as hard as possible. They were artists, mixing speeds like magicians with curves, forkballs, sliders and changeups to get and keep the hitters off-balance. As the series unraveled for the Angels, there was the occasional dugout shot of manager Gene Mauch. It was agonizing to watch. Mauch was a hell of a manager, but he had presided over what many call the most catastrophic collapse in MLB history: his 1964 Philadelphia Phillies blowing a 6 ½-game lead with just 12 games remaining - when there was no such thing as a wild card or even divisions. And here it was, happening again. When it came down to Game 5, Mauch's seasoned club had a 3-2 lead into the bottom of the seventh inning. But Cooper, with his sweetly controlled lefty swing, drilled an opposite-field, two-run single for the winning margin. The closing reliever should have been Oakland A's legend Rollie Fingers, who played his last five seasons in Milwaukee. But Fingers had torn a muscle in his forearm in September and was lost for the season. It was left to soon-to-be-forgotten Peter Ladd, who had saved only three regular-season games in his life, to finish the job. And how fitting. The incomparable Carew, who once hit .388 and won seven American League batting titles in 10 years, hit a ground ball to Yount. That was money in the bank, and the bedlam inside County Stadium spread quickly through the town. Yount played his entire 20-year career with the Brewers, and recently lamented that Uecker, who died in January 2025, won't be around for this World Series. Uecker played for the Milwaukee Braves of Henry Aaron, Eddie Mathews and Warren Spahn in 1962-63 - that team should never have left for Atlanta - and he was Milwaukee born and raised. Many beers will be raised on Uecker's behalf in the coming days. Iconic lines from the old Miller Lite ads ill be recalled, the likes of "Must be in the front row" or "Wow, they're having a good time in there." And there will be laughter. The way he liked it. Ty Majeski started on the pole, and McFarland, making his third Truck start of 2026, rolled off 24th. McFarland appeared to have avoided injury. Starting pitching depth was their biggest question in the National League Division Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Everyone knows Chris Sale is an ace, but Atlanta would benefit from more overall depth. The rest of the starting rotation features serious uncertainty. Mark Bowman of MLB.com believes Bryce Elder and Grant Holmes could make significant impacts alongside Sale next season. With that said, Bowman mentioned that adding two starters could make sense for this Braves ball club. “But when you account for the questions beyond Sale, Holmes and Elder, there’s reason to argue the Braves may need to add two starters this winter,” Bowman wrote in a recent article. item.title: Chiefs Catch Major Break as Seahawks Rule out Key Playmaker for Sunday
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 20: Zach Charbonnet #26 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up before the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 20, 2025 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Kansas City Chiefs are gearing up for a tough road matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on “Sunday Night Football” in Week 7. Kansas City will look to move to 6-0 on the season, and remain the only unbeaten team in the AFC. The Seahawks are in danger of falling under .500 with a loss, which would put them far behind the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West. Kansas City Chiefs Catch Major Break as Seahawks Rule out RB Zach Charbonnet in Week 7 Seahawks ruled out RB Zach Charbonnet for Sunday night‘s game vs the Chiefs. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 23, 2026 Despite activating him from the physically unable to perform list, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald announced on Friday that running back Zach Charbonnet will not play against the Chiefs on Sunday night. “We’re going along with the plan,” Macdonald said. “The plan was to get him a week’s worth of work and see where we’re at. It was just part of the plan.” The Seahawks led on that Charbonnet would make his season debut against Kansas City , but Macdonald threw a curveball. It’s a major break for the Chiefs, as Charbonnet is one of the best dual-threat backs in the league. Charbonnet was Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III’s backup over the past three years, often substituting in for Walker on third downs. Charbonnet has recorded 1,761 rushing yards, 693 receiving yards on 95 receptions, and 22 total touchdowns in his career. Chiefs also a bit shorthanded in Week 7 Kansas City is dealing with numerous injuries of its own. Wide receiver Rashee Rice and offensive tackle Jaylon Moore have been ruled out for Sunday night against Seattle. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed and linebacker Cooper McDonald are questionable as they battle knee ailments. Earlier this week, the Chiefs decided to place offensive tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve . Simmons has yet to play this season, and will now miss at least the next four games at minimum. He joins wide receiver Tyquan Thornton on IR, who dislocated his ankle in Week 4. Thornton will miss most of, if not the remainder of the season. Omarr Norman-Lott is currently on the PUP list, which he has been on since training camp. He is still working his way back from a torn ACL that he sustained during a Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders last season. item.title: Dodgers Fans Could See a Turbulent November
item.description: There might be an MLB lockout on the horizon, but before that is set to begin, the Los Angeles Dodgers could make some major roster changes. Teams will be able to sign free agents in the month of November, and experts told Andy McCullough of The Athletic that they think the looming shutdown will “spur activity.” Who could the Dodgers re-sign in November? To begin with, the Dodgers have nine players hitting free agency this offseason , perhaps none as impactful as Tarik Skubal. The pitcher arrived in LA just before the All-Star break and delivered on his promise, and his agent, Scott Boras, told McCullough that teams could be incentivized to act now. Aug 16, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) takes the field in the sixth inning against the Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jon Endow-Imagn Images If they wait too long, they’ll be subject to potential new rules approved in whatever deal is reached by MLB and the players union on a new collective bargaining agreement. If there’s a salary cap, for instance, it could cost players money and teams the freedom to pursue superstars. “For many teams, I can make an argument it’s clearly best for them to sign players currently, before the (new) CBA, than it is after,” agent Scott Boras said. “Because they have more freedom to do what they’re going to do. They can react later. Now they can get the talent. They can get what they want.” What other changes could the Dodgers make? This isn’t just a one-way street, though. The Dodgers will also be able to pursue free agents who played for other squads last year, and considering that many believe the Dodgers need to get younger , free agency could be a way for LA to do just that. And with the future of a potential salary cap up in the air, the Dodgers might be wise to lock down some younger talent now before they’re potentially limited from doing so in the future. Mar 15, 2025; Bunkyo, Tokyo, Japan; Hanshin Tigers right fielder Teruaki Sato (8) during the fifth inning against the Chicago Cubs at Tokyo Dome. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images For instance, could the Dodgers add another Japanese star in Teruaki Sato ? He, too, will be available to sign in November and would bring excellent hitting to a team that struggled to drive runs in this October. The Dodgers will, of course, face steep competition from other teams who also want to sign Skubal, Sato and plenty of other stars, meaning this November is shaping up to be a particularly chaotic one. Do you think the Dodgers will make big moves in November?

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
